fields.title: What makes up the bill
fields.keyTakeaway: The cost of an AI feature is determined by call frequency just as much as by call price, and the main lever is not computing what does not depend on the user at the moment of the request.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A feature costs 8 kopecks per call. Is that a lot or a little?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: AI features are the only category where prime cost can imperceptibly exceed value: the cost per call is small, but there are many calls. The calculation takes ten minutes and is done before development, not after the first invoice.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Pricing is [[price-per-1k-tokens|per token]], with input and output billed separately. Output is usually 3 to 5 times more expensive than input, but input volume is typically larger, so it dominates.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text:
call cost = input × input_price + output × output_price
yearly cost = call cost × calls per day × 365
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Additional budget items people forget about:
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Embeddings.* Both for indexing the corpus and for each query. Indexing is a one-time cost, queries are continuous. *Reranking.* An extra call for every query. *Auxiliary calls.* Query rewriting, history compression, classification. Each is a separate line item. *Retries.* Failed calls and retries are paid for.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Six reduction levers, in descending order of impact:
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **Reduce input.** Usually the largest. Fewer retrieved documents, shorter instruction, compressed history. **[[prompt-caching|Prompt caching]].** Unchanging parts are processed once. Can significantly lower input costs. **Cache answers.** Identical questions about the same product occur constantly. **[[routing|Routing]].** Simple queries to a cheap model, complex ones to an expensive model. **Reduce output.** Demand brevity in the instruction. **Compute in advance.** Review summarization does not depend on the user — it is computed in the background.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: The last lever is the most underestimated: **if the result does not depend on a specific user, it should not be computed at the moment of the request.**
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Calculation of three features before optimization:
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Summarization turned out to be the most expensive, even though it looked the simplest: it was called every time a product card was opened.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Optimization: summarization is computed once per product and recomputed when 10 new reviews accumulate. Calls dropped to 300 per day instead of 12,000. Cost fell from 2.1M to 53k per year.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Cart recommendation: reducing the catalog context from 12,400 to 3,500 tokens plus prompt caching — from 18 to 5 kopecks, 591k → 164k.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: Total savings — about 2.5M per year, while all three features remained intact.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Model prices are dropping fast, and a calculation from a year ago may be outdated. Recalculation is worth doing at every review, but the structure of levers remains stable.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: The cost of an AI feature is determined by call frequency just as much as by call price, and the main lever is not computing what does not depend on the user at the moment of the request.
